adultGuide.title: Binder Ring Story Connection Adult Guide: ____________________.
setupSteps: Set out one binder ring connection card, blank paper, pencil, and a small paper ring mark for the adult-led fictional offline paper-only session: ____________________.
Label six paper lines detail, connects to, because, second detail, bridge sentence, and binder ring check before the writer begins: ____________________.
Choose one made-up story moment from a place like Nettlewick Hall or Mallowgate Yard and keep every detail invented: ____________________.
Tell the writer that pointing, dictating, adult-scribed phrases, or short independent writing all fit this family-friendly paper activity: ____________________.
Close by rereading the bridge sentence and binder ring check from the paper card only: ____________________.
facilitationNotes: Start with one small detail so the writer has a clear paper anchor: ____________________.
Ask what the detail connects to before asking because, so the story link forms in a calm order: ____________________.
Use the because line to explain the connection with one invented reason: ____________________.
Add the second detail only after the first detail and connects to line feel clear on paper: ____________________.
Treat the binder ring check as a quiet close to the bridge sentence, not a correction mark: ____________________.
safetyNotes: Use only invented names, made-up places, pretend objects, and fictional story details: ____________________.
Skip any prompt that asks for personal facts, exact place facts, outside facts, or child identity clues: ____________________.
Keep the activity adult-led, offline, paper-only, and away from audience pressure: ____________________.
Keep every bridge sentence about the pretend story, not about a person outside the card: ____________________.
Use the binder ring check as a paper sorting mark for one fictional connection: ____________________.

connectionRoutines.title: First Detail Finder: ____________________.
connectionRoutines.useWhen: Use when the writer needs one invented detail before making a connection: ____________________.
steps: The adult points to the first detail blank on the paper card: ____________________.
The writer names one pretend object, color, sound, sign, or tiny change from the made-up story: ____________________.
The adult repeats the detail in plain words and keeps it fictional: ____________________.
The writer fills this line: My detail is ____________________.

connectionRoutines.title: Connects To Pair: ____________________.
connectionRoutines.useWhen: Use when the first detail is chosen and needs a story idea to connect to: ____________________.
steps: The adult reads the first detail from the paper card: ____________________.
The writer says what the detail connects to inside the pretend story: ____________________.
The adult asks whether the connection stays inside the made-up moment: ____________________.
The writer fills this line: My detail connects to ____________________.

connectionRoutines.title: Because Link: ____________________.
connectionRoutines.useWhen: Use when the detail connects to an idea but the reason is still missing: ____________________.
steps: The adult places the detail line beside the connects to line: ____________________.
The writer tells why the detail connects to that pretend story idea: ____________________.
The adult helps trim the because line to one clear invented phrase: ____________________.
The writer fills this line: It connects because ____________________.

connectionRoutines.title: Second Detail Support: ____________________.
connectionRoutines.useWhen: Use when one detail and because line are ready and the connection needs a second detail: ____________________.
steps: The adult rereads the detail, connects to, and because lines in order: ____________________.
The writer chooses a second detail that supports the same fictional connection: ____________________.
The adult asks how the second detail helps the same bridge sentence: ____________________.
The writer fills this line: My second detail is ____________________.

connectionRoutines.title: Bridge Sentence Build: ____________________.
connectionRoutines.useWhen: Use when the detail, connects to line, because line, and second detail are ready to combine: ____________________.
steps: The adult reads all four paper lines in order without adding outside facts: ____________________.
The writer chooses which words belong in one bridge sentence: ____________________.
The adult keeps the bridge sentence short, fictional, offline, and paper-only: ____________________.
The writer fills this line: My bridge sentence is ____________________.

connectionRoutines.title: Binder Ring Check Close: ____________________.
connectionRoutines.useWhen: Use when the bridge sentence is written and needs a final paper check: ____________________.
steps: The adult places the paper ring mark beside the bridge sentence: ____________________.
The writer points to the detail and second detail that support the sentence: ____________________.
The adult asks why the binder ring check shows a clear fictional connection: ____________________.
The writer fills this line: My binder ring check says ____________________.

takeHomeConnectionSlips.title: Detail Connects Slip: ____________________.
takeHomeConnectionSlips.adultNote: Use this slip for one adult-led fictional paper connection, with no outside facts: ____________________.

takeHomeConnectionSlips.title: Second Detail Slip: ____________________.
takeHomeConnectionSlips.prompt: My second detail is ____________________, and it supports the same connection because ____________________.
takeHomeConnectionSlips.adultNote: Ask for one more invented detail that belongs with the first detail: ____________________.

takeHomeConnectionSlips.title: Bridge Sentence Slip: ____________________.
takeHomeConnectionSlips.adultNote: Combine the detail, connects to line, because line, and second detail in one paper sentence: ____________________.

takeHomeConnectionSlips.title: Binder Ring Check Slip: ____________________.
takeHomeConnectionSlips.prompt: My binder ring check says the two details fit because ____________________.
takeHomeConnectionSlips.adultNote: Use the check as a quiet ending mark for the made-up story connection: ____________________.

takeHomeConnectionSlips.title: Tiny Connection Slip: ____________________.
takeHomeConnectionSlips.prompt: The tiniest connection I can write is ____________________ because ____________________.
takeHomeConnectionSlips.adultNote: Keep the line short so the writer can finish one adult-led paper link: ____________________.

takeHomeConnectionSlips.title: Made-Up Place Slip: ____________________.
takeHomeConnectionSlips.prompt: In ____________________, one detail connects to another detail because ____________________.
takeHomeConnectionSlips.adultNote: Use a pretend place name like Nettlewick Hall, Mallowgate Yard, or Pebblepin Pier: ____________________.

takeHomeConnectionSlips.title: Object Detail Slip: ____________________.
takeHomeConnectionSlips.prompt: The object detail ____________________ connects to the story idea ____________________ because ____________________.
takeHomeConnectionSlips.adultNote: Choose a pretend object and keep the connection inside the fictional moment: ____________________.

takeHomeConnectionSlips.title: Character Thought Slip: ____________________.
takeHomeConnectionSlips.prompt: A made-up character might think ____________________ because the detail ____________________ connects to ____________________.
takeHomeConnectionSlips.adultNote: Keep the thought invented and tied to the paper detail: ____________________.

takeHomeConnectionSlips.title: Two Detail Pair Slip: ____________________.
takeHomeConnectionSlips.adultNote: Read both details before asking for the bridge sentence: ____________________.

takeHomeConnectionSlips.title: Later Ring Slip: ____________________.
takeHomeConnectionSlips.prompt: Next paper session, I can add one new detail that connects to ____________________.
takeHomeConnectionSlips.adultNote: Save this as a family-friendly offline paper-only starter for another adult-led connection: ____________________.

optionalAdultPrompts: Which small detail can start this adult-led fictional paper connection: ____________________.
What does the detail connects to inside the made-up story moment: ____________________.
Why does the detail connect because of something already on the card: ____________________.
What second detail supports the same story connection: ____________________.
Which words make a clear bridge sentence from the two details: ____________________.
Where should the binder ring check sit beside the bridge sentence: ____________________.
Which blank can stay empty until the writer is ready to dictate or write: ____________________.
What invented detail can be saved for the next offline paper-only connection: ____________________.
